results: Including scVI in a matched empirical specification analysis did not yield a detectable pooled association (Supplementary Fig. S17; Supplementary Table S17). The same encoding rules produced 20 binary features, including three features specific to scVI, while leaving all original eight-method Jaccard distances unchanged. The original empirical result was reproduced with a Mantel Spearman correlation of 0.164 and exact P = 0.475. Uniform rescoring gave 0.148 and P = 0.526 for the eight anchors, compared with 0.125, P = 0.510 and adjusted q = 0.927 for the nine-method pooled profile. The heart-subset association was stronger descriptively at 0.369, but its exact P = 0.030 became q = 0.119 after correction across the pooled and three context tests. None of the six alternative encodings retained a detected association after their separate exploratory correction. Method omissions and endpoint omissions revealed sensitivity to the composition of the comparison; they were not used to select a favourable subset. These post hoc results do not demonstrate absence of an association or representativeness of all 26 methods.
methods: The nine-method specification analysis was a post hoc revision sensitivity analysis using the full-object seed-zero, two-dimensional diagnostics reported in Supplementary Fig. S16. Each method contributed local retention, trustworthiness, global-rank correlation and same-label neighbour fraction in PBMC3k, Paul15 and the heart subset. The nine methods shared PCA50, k = 15 and 5,000 valid non-self distance pairs sampled with seed 20261005. The observation-model, latent-parameterisation and active-objective fields were encoded using the original rules, including the scScope projection-stage and reconstruction-only SAUCIE adjustments. The nine-method union contained 20 features rather than 17; the additions were negative-binomial count observations, variational encoder with neural decoder and latent prior. The eight-anchor Jaccard submatrix was required to remain identical. Twelve-variable pooled profiles and four-variable context profiles were standardised across the methods evaluated in each comparison. Profile distance was Euclidean distance divided by the square root of the number of variables. The original eight-method calculation, the uniformly rescored eight-method control and the matched nine-method extension were reported separately. Missing, duplicate or non-finite required values caused the analysis to stop; none were imputed or excluded selectively.

Exact two-sided Mantel Spearman tests reassigned whole empirical profiles to fixed specification records under the null of exchangeable correspondence across the evaluated configurations. All 40,320 assignments were enumerated for eight methods and all 362,880 for nine, including the observed assignment. Average ranks handled tied distances; the exact probability was the fraction with absolute correlation at least as large as observed, using a numerical tolerance of 0.000000000001 and no Monte Carlo plus-one correction. The pooled nine-method and three context tests formed one four-test Benjamini-Hochberg family. Six alternative encodings formed a separate exploratory family. Method omissions were calculated both with fixed full-nine scaling and with restandardisation within each eight-method subset. Omissions of individual diagnostics or datasets were descriptive influence analyses. Their shared observations are not independent replicates, and the contrast between two correlations was not tested as a difference. Central 95% permutation intervals describe the null reference, not confidence intervals. Inference is conditional on nine selected configurations and three fixed contexts, not a randomly sampled population of methods. The original eight-method specification tests and six-scenario simulations were retained unchanged (Supplementary Fig. S17; Supplementary Table S17).
legend: Supplementary Fig. S17. Adding scVI does not yield a detected pooled specification-profile association. This post hoc sensitivity uses the nine seed-zero, two-dimensional representations scored identically in Supplementary Fig. S16. The full PBMC3k, Paul15 and heart objects contain 2,638, 2,730 and 8,000 cells, respectively; PCA50, k = 15 and 5,000 fixed non-self pairs are shared within each context. a, Jaccard distance between 20-feature specification records versus pooled empirical-profile distance. Grey circles denote 28 anchor pairs and blue diamonds the eight pairs containing scVI. RMS z denotes Euclidean distance divided by the square root of 12 column-standardised context-by-diagnostic variables. These 36 pair dots are dependent; n is nine evaluated methods, not 36 independent observations. b, Original eight-method, uniformly rescored eight-method and rescored nine-method associations. Dots are observed Mantel Spearman correlations; grey bars are central 95% exact permutation references, not confidence intervals. P values are exact two-sided method-label probabilities. The eight-method controls distinguish changes in distance-pair sampling from method inclusion; their correlations are not tested against one another. c, Context-specific four-variable profiles. Blue, green and purple denote PBMC3k, Paul15 and heart atlas. The dashed line is the pooled nine-method correlation. P is unadjusted; q uses Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the pooled and three context tests. d, Six alternative specification encodings. Green dots are correlations; the right column gives q values from a separate six-test exploratory correction. Flags omitted removes not-explicit indicators, not unavailable measurements. The dashed line is primary Jaccard encoding. e, Leave-one-method-out correlations, using fixed nine-method scaling (blue circles) or rescaled eight-method subsets (orange squares). Grey segments join the paired calculations; the dashed line is the complete nine-method result. f, Change in correlation after omitting one diagnostic block (green) or one dataset block (pink). Local, Trust, Global and Same-label denote reference-neighbour overlap, trustworthiness, distance-rank correlation and same-label neighbour fraction. Zero denotes no change from the pooled result. e and f are descriptive influence diagnostics, not causal effects or independent confirmatory tests. Tests enumerate all 40,320 or 362,880 whole-method assignments for eight or nine methods, respectively, with average ranks for ties. No biological replicate inference or significance symbols are used. Complete measurements, effects, exact tail counts, probabilities and influence results are reported in Supplementary Tables S16 and S17.
table_caption: Supplementary Table S17. Nine-method specification-profile association and sensitivity results. Rows report pair distances, original and rescored controls, pooled and context-specific tests, six alternative encodings, method omissions under two scaling rules and diagnostic or dataset omissions. Specification distance is Jaccard distance over the union of 20 binary observation-model, latent-model and active-objective features; profile distance is Euclidean distance divided by the square root of the number of standardised variables. The pooled profile uses four diagnostics in each of three contexts. All matched results use full objects, two-dimensional seed-zero coordinates, PCA50, k = 15 and 5,000 fixed non-self pairs. n methods is the permutation unit; pair distances are dependent. P exact is the two-sided whole-method Mantel Spearman probability, including all assignments. q BH applies only to the stated four-test pooled/context or six-test exploratory family. Null lower/upper 95 are central permutation reference limits, not confidence limits. Omissions are descriptive, and their raw probabilities are not corrected confirmatory claims. Delta rho is the omitted-block correlation minus the pooled nine-method value. No missing diagnostic was imputed. The original eight-method simulation analysis is not extended to scVI.
